Miasma/Shai-Hulud typosquat PyPI package installation (rsquests, tlask, langchain-core-mcp, durabletask) AIDelivery High
Detects pip / uv / poetry installing the named-and-shamed packages from the Miasma supply-chain campaign — Python typosquats of requests/flask, MCP/AI-themed lures, and the originally-compromised durabletask. Catches the initial install before .pth/.abi3.so payload runs. Rationale: Hard-coded against the exact 19-package list named in the article body (the new wave plus the original durabletask). Bracketing on pip/uv/poetry parents avoids matching when the package name simply appears in a doc string or chat log. Cross-checked with Socket public advisories on the Shai-Hulud / Hades wave. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-restores-some-github-repos.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal package mirror sync replicating the malicious versions before they were yanked
  • Security researcher / IR team reproducing the campaign in a lab (should originate from a sandbox VM)
  • Pip dry-run / pip download (downloads but does not install) — pivot on `download` vs `install` verb if needed
  • CI build that pinned a vulnerable version pre-disclosure and hasn't updated requirements.txt
  • Developer reading article and copy-pasting package names into a notes file (process will be notepad/cmd, not pip)
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has " download " and ProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full ProcessCommandLine — confirm `install` (not `download`/`search`) and identify exact version. Cross-check version against article's named bad versions (e.g. rsquests 2.34.3, tlask 3.1.4). 2. Contain: Isolate the developer's workstation; revoke any GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access key, GCP service-account JSON, SSH key, and .env secrets present on the host (those are the Miasma stealer's known exfil targets). Pull the user's GitHub account for any new public repos created in the last 7 days — that is the campaign's exfil channel. 3. Hunt: Search Network Resolution DNS for any beacon to the three IOC domains from the same host; search FileEvents for `_index.js`, `.pth` writes in site-packages, and `.abi3.so` writes; check for `bun.exe` execution as child of python.

Miasma loader artifact written to Python site-packages: .pth, _index.js, .abi3.so AIInstallation High
Detects file creation of the three Miasma payload-delivery artifact types inside any Python site-packages directory: executable .pth startup hooks, the _index.js JavaScript stealer payload, and trojanized native .abi3.so extensions that execute on import. Rationale: Article enumerates three distinct loader shapes: (1) executable .pth startup hooks bootstrapping Bun, (2) trojanized .abi3.so native extensions that run on import, (3) .pth variant that searches sys.path for _index.js. The site-packages path + pip/python writer narrows to package-install context, dropping editor file-saves and noise from non-Python ecosystems. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/
ATT&CKT1546 T1574
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate packages with .pth files (setuptools, pytest, easy-install.pth) — extremely common; filter by file name patterns or hash baseline
  • Legitimate native extensions (.abi3.so) being installed for legitimate scientific packages (numpy, scipy, pyarrow)
  • An internal package mirror replaying a legitimate install for IT-managed Python builds
  • Developer manually crafting a .pth file for editable installs (pip install -e .)
  • Conda/mamba activity if the team uses conda envs that overlap with pip site-packages
Suppression filter
| where not(FileName in~ ("easy-install.pth","distutils-precedence.pth","setuptools.pth","pip-runner.pth"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Read the .pth file contents (one-liner — must start with `import`). If it imports an obfuscated module or references a JS payload (`_index.js`), it is Miasma. For .abi3.so, hash and check against article SHA256s + VirusTotal. 2. Contain: Quarantine the file, uninstall the parent package (`pip uninstall <pkg>`), and isolate the developer workstation. Treat any secret material on the host as compromised — revoke GitHub PATs, AWS keys, npm tokens, .env contents. 3. Hunt: Pull all FileEvents in the user's site-packages dirs for the last 90 days for the same payload patterns; pull bun.exe execution; check the user's GitHub account for newly-created public repos (exfil destination).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has @"\site-packages\" or FolderPath has "/site-packages/"
| where FileName endswith ".pth" or FileName =~ "_index.js" or FileName endswith ".abi3.so"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\site-packages\" or TargetFilePath has "/site-packages/"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".pth" or TargetFileName =~ "_index.js" or TargetFileName endswith ".abi3.so"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "pip.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "python.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "python3.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "uv.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "poetry.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun or Node runtime spawned by Python package manager (Miasma stealer bootstrap) AIInstallation High
Detects Bun JS runtime (or node.exe) launched as a child of pip / python / uv / poetry. Article: Miasma .pth startup hooks bootstrap Bun and run an obfuscated JavaScript stealer when the package is imported on a developer workstation or CI runner. Rationale: Article: Bun is the article-specific runtime used to execute the obfuscated JavaScript stealer after the .pth startup hook fires. python→bun parent/child is an inherently anomalous tree — Python packages do not legitimately spawn Bun. Combined with Sentinel ImProcessCreate's ParentProcessName field, this is single-event-shape detection with low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer's Python project that legitimately shells out to bun/node for a build step (rare — typically reversed: node spawns python)
  • Jupyter notebook with `!bun run ...` cells (parent is python kernel)
  • CI runner where pytest exec-spawns node for a JS-side integration test
  • Internal tooling that uses subprocess to wrap node-based linting from python wrappers
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has " -m pytest" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "jupyter"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull bun ProcessCommandLine — Miasma invokes Bun against `_index.js` or against a path inside the user's site-packages. Hash the script Bun is running and check against the article SHA256s. 2. Contain: Kill bun + parent python process trees, isolate the host. Treat all developer secrets as compromised — rotate GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access keys, .env contents, ssh keys, kubeconfig, gcp service-account JSON. 3. Hunt: Pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents from the same host within ±10 minutes for the three Miasma IOC domains; pivot to DeviceFileEvents for site-packages writes of _index.js / .pth / .abi3.so; check the user's GitHub account for new public repo creations in the last 7 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun","node.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pip.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "python.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "python3.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "pip.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "uv.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "poetry.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun or Node Runtime Spawned by Python Package Manager (Miasma)
id: f8a2c3b4-9d6e-4f1a-b7c5-3d2e8a9f1b56
description: Detects the Bun JavaScript runtime (or Node.js) executed as a child of pip / python / uv / poetry. Miasma campaign .pth startup hooks bootstrap Bun to run the _index.js stealer after a trojanized Python package is imported.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-restores-some-github-repos.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
  condition: child and parent
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1) AND @Image:(*\bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE OR *\Bun.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\Node.exe) AND @ParentImage:(*\python.exe OR *\PYTHON.EXE OR *\Python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\pip.exe OR *\PIP.EXE OR *\uv.exe OR *\poetry.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(bun|node)\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/(python|python3|pip|uv|poetry)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun","node.exe") Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","pip.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe") by host user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun","node.exe") Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","pip.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe") by host user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Miasma stealer payload SHA256 match on disk or in execution AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based detection for the two specific SHA256 IOCs tied to the Miasma campaign JavaScript stealer payload. Catches the payload regardless of file name or path, including renamed or moved copies. Rationale: Pre-extracted SHA256 IOCs from the article body. Hash-based detection is the canonical low-FP signature for a known-bad binary; this complements the behavioural UCs above and catches the payload if attackers reshape delivery (rename .pth/.so, change domains) but keep the stealer body. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-restores-some-github-repos.html
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonation (analyst lab host)
  • AV/EDR submission of the file for analysis
  • Forensic copy of the file being moved off a quarantined host
  • Researcher pulling a sample from VirusTotal for analysis
  • Reverse-engineering lab VM with the sample staged for study
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm the host is not a sandbox/lab/IR machine. Pull SHA256-matching FileEvents history and process trees for full chain. 2. Contain: Isolate the host immediately; the hash match indicates payload execution or staging. Rotate ALL developer secrets on the host (GitHub PAT, npm, AWS, GCP, .env, ssh, kubeconfig). Submit hash to Defender Custom Indicator block list. 3. Hunt: Search the org for both hashes across DeviceFileEvents/DeviceProcessEvents for the last 90 days; pull the user's GitHub for new public repos (exfil channel); check CI/CD runner logs for the same hashes if developer pushed code that triggered builds.
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic(["6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2"]);
union
  ( DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (MiasmaHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EventSource = "Process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine ),
  ( DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventSource = "File", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic(["6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in (MiasmaHashes) or Hash in (MiasmaHashes)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Supply Chain Stealer Payload Hash Match
id: b6f3d8e1-2a47-4c9d-8e1f-5b9c2a3d4f78
description: Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the SHA256 hashes attributed to the Miasma / Shai-Hulud supply chain campaign JavaScript stealer payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-restores-some-github-repos.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9'
      - '6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2'
  condition: selection
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender OR windows.security) AND @Hashes:(*6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9* OR *6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2*)
SHA256HashData=/^(6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9|6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") OR Processes.parent_process_hash IN ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") by host user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") OR Processes.parent_process_hash IN ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9","6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") by host user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") or SHA1 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") or MD5 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") or SHA1 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2") or MD5 in~ ("6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6d332f814f15f19758d65026bbfd0a8c49671b319ec77b8fa1b27fc48afff7d9", "6506d31707a39949f89534bf9705bcf889f1ecae3dbc6f4ff88d67a8be3d01b2"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Unpatched Chrome vulnerable to CVE-2026-11645 and 2026 in-the-wild zero-days AIExploitation High
Identifies endpoints reporting Chrome installations vulnerable to CVE-2026-11645 and the four prior actively-exploited Chrome zero-days disclosed in 2026 (CVE-2026-2441/-3909/-3910/-5281). Posture hunt, not a behavioural alert — drives patch enforcement before drive-by exploitation lands. Rationale: Pivots exclusively on the five Chrome CVE IDs the article explicitly enumerates (CVE-2026-11645 plus the four other 2026 ITW Chrome zero-days: 2441/3909/3910/5281). TVM-driven posture hunt rather than behavioural detection because Google withheld exploit specifics. Joins to inventory to surface the actual installed version operators need to drive patch enforcement.
ATT&CKT1189 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Device just auto-updated but TVM snapshot is from prior scan (eventual-consistency lag, typically <24h)
  • Chrome for Business pinned to an enterprise channel under MDM policy — vulnerable but intentionally held back pending stability validation
  • Air-gapped lab/OT endpoint that legitimately can't reach Google update servers
  • Chromium-derived browsers (Brave/Edge/Vivaldi) misidentified by vendor inventory normalisation as 'Google Chrome'
  • Portable Chrome distribution installed under a user profile that TVM tracks separately from the system install
Suppression filter
| where InstalledVersion !startswith "149.0.7827.10" or toint(extract(@"^149\.0\.7827\.(\d+)", 1, InstalledVersion)) < 102
Response runbook
1. Triage: enumerate hits by device + installed version; confirm hits aren't already on 149.0.7827.102/.103 with a fresh AV/EDR check-in (TVM lag is the #1 FP). 2. Contain: push the Chrome update via Intune/SCCM/Workspace ONE; for managed Chrome, force the relaunch via the RelaunchNotification enterprise policy. Block file downloads from untrusted origins until patch confirmed. 3. Hunt: for any device that was unpatched during the exposure window, pivot to DeviceProcessEvents/DeviceNetworkEvents on chrome.exe spawning non-browser children or unusual outbound destinations during that window — V8 RCE inside the sandbox plus a separate sandbox-escape is the historical pattern for in-the-wild Chrome chains.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281")
| where SoftwareName has "chrome" or SoftwareVendor has "google"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has "chrome"
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, SoftwareVersion, EndOfSupportStatus) by DeviceId, SoftwareName
  ) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, InstalledVersion=SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, Timestamp desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281")
| where SoftwareName has "chrome" or SoftwareVendor has "google"
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId, CveId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.cvss | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)` | `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)` | sort - cvss
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.cvss | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)` | `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)` | sort - cvss
Chrome process executing with pre-fix V8 version (149.0.7827.<102) post-disclosure AIExploitation Medium
Detects chrome.exe processes whose runtime ProductVersion is below the fixed build (149.0.7827.102 Linux / .102-.103 Win+Mac) after the 2026-06-09 disclosure. Catches the residual-risk window where Chrome auto-updated the on-disk binary but the user has not yet relaunched — the running process is still vulnerable to in-the-wild CVE-2026-11645 exploitation. Rationale: Uses the exact patched-version threshold the article specifies (149.0.7827.102 Linux / .102-.103 Windows+macOS). Different telemetry source from UC1 — process-runtime ProductVersion rather than vuln-mgmt snapshot — so it catches the gap between 'binary updated on disk' and 'user actually relaunched browser', which is where in-the-wild exploitation of disclosed zero-days actually lands in real environments.
ATT&CKT1189 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User has tabs open and hasn't relaunched after Chrome auto-updated the binary — exact intended-hit, but operationally an FP for 'is the install vulnerable'
  • Chrome Beta / Dev / Canary channels using older or higher-numbered version schemes that confuse the major.build.patch comparator
  • Electron / CEF-embedded apps that emit chrome.exe-like ProductVersion strings but aren't the user's browsing surface (Slack, Teams, VS Code helpers)
  • Portable Chrome builds (PortableApps, ChromeStandaloneSetup) running off USB / user profile that lag the managed-install update cadence
  • Older Chrome milestones still on M148 LTS / Chrome for Business extended-stable channel under enterprise pinning policy
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Microsoft\\Teams\\","\\slack\\","\\Discord\\","\\Code\\","\\Postman\\","\\GitHub Desktop\\")) | where not (ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("Beta","Canary","Dev","Electron"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: filter results to the actual Stable channel (exclude ProcessVersionInfoProductName matching 'Beta'/'Dev'/'Canary') and Electron-style helper processes (cross-reference FolderPath against the canonical install dirs C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application and /Applications/Google Chrome.app). 2. Contain: push a forced Chrome relaunch via enterprise RelaunchNotification policy (Recommended=14d minimum, set to Required for this CVE) or send targeted user comms via your EUC channel. 3. Hunt: for any device that ran a vulnerable Chrome process during the exposure window, sweep DeviceProcessEvents for chrome.exe spawning non-Chromium children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, mshta.exe) and DeviceNetworkEvents for chrome.exe connections to first-seen-in-org domains during that window.
let FixedMajor = 149;
let FixedBuild = 7827;
let FixedPatch = 102;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > datetime(2026-06-09)
| where FileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Google"
| where isnotempty(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion)
| extend Parts = split(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Build = toint(Parts[2]), Patch = toint(Parts[3])
| where isnotnull(Major) and isnotnull(Build) and isnotnull(Patch)
| where (Major < FixedMajor)
     or (Major == FixedMajor and Minor == 0 and Build < FixedBuild)
     or (Major == FixedMajor and Minor == 0 and Build == FixedBuild and Patch < FixedPatch)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), ExecCount=count(), AnyCmd=any(ProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
let FixedMajor = 149;
let FixedBuild = 7827;
let FixedPatch = 102;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > datetime(2026-06-09)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "chrome.exe"
| where TargetProcessFileCompany has "Google" or ActingProcessFileCompany has "Google"
| extend ChromeVer = tostring(coalesce(column_ifexists("TargetProcessFileVersion", ""), ActingProcessFileVersion))
| where isnotempty(ChromeVer)
| extend Parts = split(ChromeVer, ".")
| extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Build = toint(Parts[2]), Patch = toint(Parts[3])
| where isnotnull(Major) and isnotnull(Build) and isnotnull(Patch)
| where (Major < FixedMajor)
     or (Major == FixedMajor and Minor == 0 and Build < FixedBuild)
     or (Major == FixedMajor and Minor == 0 and Build == FixedBuild and Patch < FixedPatch)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), ExecCount=count() by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ChromeVer
| order by LastSeen desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process_version) as process_version from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=chrome.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_version | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process_version, "^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$") | rex field=process_version "^(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<build>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)$" | eval major=tonumber(major), minor=tonumber(minor), build=tonumber(build), patch=tonumber(patch) | where (major<149) OR (major=149 AND minor=0 AND build<7827) OR (major=149 AND minor=0 AND build=7827 AND patch<102) | `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)` | `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)` | sort - lastSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process_version) as process_version from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=chrome.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_version | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process_version, "^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$") | rex field=process_version "^(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<build>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)$" | eval major=tonumber(major), minor=tonumber(minor), build=tonumber(build), patch=tonumber(patch) | where (major<149) OR (major=149 AND minor=0 AND build<7827) OR (major=149 AND minor=0 AND build=7827 AND patch<102) | `security_content_ctime(firstSeen)` | `security_content_ctime(lastSeen)` | sort - lastSeen
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.128.228.6", "104.207.144.154", "146.19.216.119", "146.19.216.120", "146.19.216.125", "179.43.172.213", "185.195.232.139", "198.12.106.60", "202.144.192.47", "209.99.191.137", "79.130.26.202") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["23.128.228.6", "104.207.144.154", "146.19.216.119", "146.19.216.120", "146.19.216.125", "179.43.172.213", "185.195.232.139", "198.12.106.60", "202.144.192.47", "209.99.191.137", "79.130.26.202"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-0257")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-0257")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Miasma Phantom Gyp: python.exe (gyp parser) spawning node index.js during npm install AIInstallation High
Detects the core Miasma v2 abuse where node-gyp's Python parser executes a GYP command-expansion (<!(...)>) embedded in binding.gyp, spawning the credential-stealer payload as a child of python.exe rather than via package.json lifecycle hooks. Hunts the specific parent→child shape the worm produces during dependency install. Rationale: Anchored on the exact process tree the article describes: node-gyp invokes Python (gyp.py) to parse binding.gyp, and the embedded <!(node index.js > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo stub.c) command spawns node.exe with index.js as a direct child of python.exe — a parent→child shape that legitimate native add-on builds never produce (those go python→cl.exe/link.exe/cmake.exe). Allow-list of real toolchain children suppresses normal node-gyp activity. Cross-checked Semgrep, Endor Labs, StepSecurity write-ups confirming the python→node payload chain. Cross-checked against: • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/malicious-payload-in-ai-sdk-ollama-npm-package • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm • https://corgea.com/research/miasma-phantom-gyp-npm-worm-vapi-ai-sdk-ollama-june-2026
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate packages (e.g. node-pre-gyp, node-sass forks) where binding.gyp uses <!(node -e '...') to probe Node/Python versions at configure time
  • Developers running 'node-gyp rebuild --verbose' manually during native-addon debugging on a developer workstation
  • CI agents building Electron / better-sqlite3 / canvas / sharp where the configure step invokes node helpers (rare but possible)
  • Internal tooling that wraps node-gyp with custom Python pre-processors for cross-compilation
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-pre-gyp","--target_platform","--target_arch") and ProcessCommandLine has "-e" and ProcessCommandLine has "process.version")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full process tree (npm.cmd → node.exe → python.exe → matching child). Inspect the binding.gyp at the parent's working directory (look for <!(...), <!@(...), or pymod_do_main tokens); review the child's command line for 'index.js' or sandbox-escape Python literals. Confirm which npm package owns the node_modules subdirectory the binding.gyp came from. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host from network, revoke any npm/GitHub/AWS/GCP/Azure/Vault tokens that resided on it (Miasma harvests all of these), force-rotate the developer's npm 2FA recovery codes, and pause CI runners using the same npm cache. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountObjectId across DeviceFileEvents for reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml in the same window; check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to api.github.com / *.workers.dev from that node.exe PID; review npm audit log and GitHub audit log for any package republicatio
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","node-gyp","binding.gyp","gyp_main")
| where FileName !in~ ("cl.exe","link.exe","cmake.exe","msbuild.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","clang.exe","clang++.exe","make.exe","nmake.exe","ld.exe","tracker.exe","rc.exe","cvtres.exe","mt.exe","conhost.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node","cmd.exe","sh","bash","dash","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("index.js","__subclasses__","catch_warnings","echo stub.c","/dev/null 2>&1","__import__('os')","pymod_do_main")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("node_modules","npm-cache","_npx","yarn","pnpm") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]python3?(\.exe)?$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","node-gyp","binding.gyp","gyp_main")
| where not(ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](cl|link|cmake|msbuild|gcc|g\+\+|clang|clang\+\+|make|nmake|ld|tracker|rc|cvtres|mt|conhost)\.exe$")
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](node|cmd|sh|bash|dash|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh)(\.exe)?$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("index.js","__subclasses__","catch_warnings","echo stub.c","/dev/null 2>&1","__import__('os')","pymod_do_main")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256
title: Miasma Phantom Gyp - Python gyp parser spawning Node payload via binding.gyp
id: 7f3b6c2a-d4e1-4a01-9c5e-3a4f1c8e7b22
description: Detects node-gyp's Python parser (gyp.py) spawning unexpected child processes during npm install, indicative of GYP command-expansion abuse used by the Miasma v2 / Phantom Gyp worm (June 2026)
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/exploring-binding-gyp-npm-build-system
  - https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/
  - https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/malicious-payload-in-ai-sdk-ollama-npm-package
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_python_gyp:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'gyp.py'
      - 'node-gyp'
      - 'binding.gyp'
  suspicious_child_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  suspicious_child_cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'index.js'
      - '__subclasses__'
      - 'catch_warnings'
      - 'echo stub.c'
      - "__import__('os')"
      - 'pymod_do_main'
  filter_compilers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cl.exe'
      - '\link.exe'
      - '\cmake.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
      - '\gcc.exe'
      - '\clang.exe'
      - '\make.exe'
      - '\nmake.exe'
  condition: parent_python_gyp and (suspicious_child_image or suspicious_child_cmdline) and not filter_compilers
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate packages whose binding.gyp uses <!(node ...) for non-malicious build-time configuration (e.g. node-pre-gyp version probing)
  - Developers manually invoking node-gyp rebuild for native add-on debugging
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\PYTHON.EXE OR *\\python3.exe) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*gyp.py* OR *node-gyp* OR *binding.gyp*)) AND (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*index.js* OR *__subclasses__* OR *catch_warnings* OR *"echo stub.c"* OR *pymod_do_main* OR *__import__* )) AND -@Image:(*\\cl.exe OR *\\link.exe OR *\\cmake.exe OR *\\msbuild.exe OR *\\gcc.exe OR *\\clang.exe OR *\\make.exe OR *\\nmake.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^python3?\.exe$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/(gyp\.py|node-gyp|binding\.gyp|gyp_main)/i
| (ImageFileName=/\\(node|cmd|sh|bash|dash|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(index\.js|__subclasses__|catch_warnings|echo stub\.c|\/dev\/null 2>&1|__import__\('os'\)|pymod_do_main)/i)
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(cl|link|cmake|msbuild|gcc|g\+\+|clang|clang\+\+|make|nmake|ld|tracker|rc|cvtres|mt)\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/

Miasma-tainted package install: binding.gyp dropped into known-compromised npm package paths AIDelivery High
File-event detection for binding.gyp files written into node_modules subdirectories of the publicly named Miasma v2 victims (@vapi-ai/server-sdk, ai-sdk-ollama, @redhat-cloud-services/*). These packages historically had no native add-on, so the mere presence of binding.gyp inside their node_modules path is the campaign signature. Rationale: The article explicitly names @vapi-ai/server-sdk (71k weekly downloads) and ai-sdk-ollama (31k weekly downloads) as victims and references the @redhat-cloud-services namespace; corroborating sources confirm these packages historically had no native code, so binding.gyp inside their tree is the campaign signature. Detection is path-anchored to those exact package names rather than generic binding.gyp activity. Cross-checked Semgrep, Chainguard, and Endor Labs. Cross-checked against: • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://www.chainguard.dev/unchained/chainguard-artifacts-safe-from-miasma-phantom-gyp-npm-attack • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/malicious-payload-in-ai-sdk-ollama-npm-package
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1505.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A vendor-published clean (post-incident) version of one of these packages ships a legitimate binding.gyp — verify file hash against the npm registry tarball
  • Local file restore from backup containing an old node_modules tree
  • Forensic copy / IR engineer staging the malicious sample onto a sandbox host for analysis
  • A developer cloning the repo (not via npm) where a legitimate maintainer added a build-time helper in binding.gyp
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the dropped binding.gyp content (extract from disk or EDR file-capture) and confirm it contains <!(...), <!@(...), pymod_do_main, or Python sandbox-escape literals (__subclasses__, catch_warnings). Confirm the installed package version matches the IOC range (@vapi-ai/server-sdk >0.11.0, ai-sdk-ollama >0.13.0). Step 2 — Contain: stop any in-flight node-gyp rebuild PID, isolate the host, and treat ALL credentials reachable from the host as burned — npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS/GCP/Azure CLI configs, kubeconfigs, Vault tokens, .npmrc auth. Trigger automated rotation. Step 3 — Hunt: query all hosts and CI runners for the same package-path pattern in the last 14 days; check the maintainer's npm account for unauthorized package republications via npm audit logs; review GitHub org for newly created repos under the developer's account (Miasma uses GitHub for dead-drop exfil).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (
    @"node_modules\@vapi-ai\server-sdk",
    "node_modules/@vapi-ai/server-sdk",
    @"node_modules\ai-sdk-ollama",
    "node_modules/ai-sdk-ollama",
    @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services",
    "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("git.exe","code.exe","explorer.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (
    @"node_modules\@vapi-ai\server-sdk",
    "node_modules/@vapi-ai/server-sdk",
    @"node_modules\ai-sdk-ollama",
    "node_modules/ai-sdk-ollama",
    @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services",
    "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

Miasma payload SHA256 hash hit (published Phantom Gyp IOCs) AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based match for the four SHA256s associated with the Miasma v2 Phantom Gyp payload set. Fires on either file write or process execution telemetry. Universal IOC sweep across endpoint estate. Rationale: Direct hash IOC sweep against the four SHA256s the article ships. Hash detections are non-negotiable for any campaign with published IOCs — universal, low-FP, and works across file-event and process-event surfaces. Coverage spans both DeviceFileEvents (catches the dropped artifact even if it never executes) and DeviceProcessEvents (catches execution attempts). Cross-checked against: • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forensic analyst or malware researcher intentionally placing the IOC sample on a sandbox / detonation host
  • Security tooling (e.g. EDR test harness, YARA-rule unit test fixtures) staging the hash for validation
  • Threat-intel platform pre-caching the file for hash-lookup tests
  • Inbound email or chat attachment carrying the sample for IR analysis (will hit Defender mail scan first)
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("SOC-SANDBOX-01","IR-WORKSTATION-01","MALWARE-LAB-01")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the host is not a sanctioned forensic / sandbox / IR-analyst workstation by checking the device tag and the user's role in IdentityInfo. Pull the full file path and parent process for the hash hit; if it executed (DeviceProcessEvents row), the host is presumed compromised. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the device immediately via Live Response / Defender machine action, suspend the user's npm / GitHub / cloud sessions, kill the offending PID. Treat all secrets reachable from the host as burned and force rotation (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS keys, .npmrc auth, kubeconfig, Vault tokens). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountObjectId and SHA256 across the full estate for the last 30 days; check whether any package on npm under the user's maintainer account was published in the same window (Miasma republishes from victim hosts); review GitHub audit log for new repos under the user's account in the last 7 days (potential dead-drop exfil endpoint).
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic([
  "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90",

  "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108"
]);
union
  ( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
    | project Timestamp, Source="FileEvent", DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Path=FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
  ( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
    | project Timestamp, Source="ProcessEvent", DeviceName, AccountName, Path=FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic([

Node child of node-gyp/python making outbound to GitHub dead-drop or anomalous web service during install AIexfil Medium
Catches the Miasma exfiltration step: after the binding.gyp command-expansion fires, the spawned node.exe (running index.js) beacons cloud credentials and CI tokens out to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories or webhook services. Pivots on the rare combination of node.exe with a node-gyp/python ancestor making outbound TCP to api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, or first-seen external hosts. Rationale: Anchors on the article's described post-execution behavior (credential exfil to attacker-controlled dead-drops) with the parent-process chain unique to binding.gyp abuse. Corroborating sources (Endor Labs, Morphisec, OX Security) confirm Miasma exfils to GitHub dead-drop repos and uses Workers/webhook bouncers; this detection requires both the gyp ancestry AND the suspicious destination to fire, keeping FPs manageable while catching the campaign-specific exfil shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/malicious-payload-in-ai-sdk-ollama-npm-package • https://www.morphisec.com/blog/its-in-your-ai-assistant-now-shai-hulud-wave-3-and-the-miasma-worm-targeting-npm/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/600000-monthly-downloads-affected-miasma-supply-chain-attack-is-back-on-npm/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1552.001 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm packages whose postinstall hook fetches assets from raw.githubusercontent.com (e.g. node-pre-gyp downloading prebuilt binaries) — but those typically run as direct child of npm, not via python.exe (gyp) chain
  • node-gyp packages that pull source tarballs from GitHub during configure step (rare; node-pre-gyp uses HTTP downloader)
  • CI runners that genuinely push to api.github.com via node-based GitHub API client called from a build hook
  • Cloudflare Workers used by an org's internal build accelerator service
Suppression filter
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-pre-gyp","prebuild-install") and DstHostname has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the spawning binding.gyp content and the node process's full argv; identify which npm package owns the source path. Check whether the GitHub destination repo is org-controlled (legitimate) or an externally owned account (likely dead-drop). Step 2 — Contain: kill the node.exe PID, isolate the device, and immediately rotate every credential reachable from the host — focus first on the developer's GitHub PAT (worm publishes via it), npm publish token, AWS keys in ~/.aws/credentials, .npmrc auth, kubeconfig, Vault tokens, GCP/Azure CLI cache. Step 3 — Hunt: query GitHub audit log for new repository creations under the developer's user account in the last 24h (Miasma creates ephemeral dead-drop repos); search ImNetworkSession for any other node.exe egress to the same destination from CI runners in the last 7 days; check npm registry for unauthorized package publications under the dev's maintainer accounts.
let gyp_node_children = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","cmd.exe","sh","bash")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","binding.gyp","node-gyp")
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project ProcSpawnTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com",".workers.dev","webhook.site","ngrok.io","hooks.slack.com","discord.com/api/webhooks","transfer.sh","file.io","0x0.st")
   or RemoteIPType == "Public"
| join kind=inner gyp_node_children on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| where Timestamp between (ProcSpawnTime .. ProcSpawnTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, GypParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine1
| order by Timestamp desc
let gyp_node_children = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]node(\.exe)?$"
    | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](python3?|cmd|sh|bash)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","binding.gyp","node-gyp")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project ProcSpawnTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstHostname has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com",".workers.dev","webhook.site","ngrok.io","hooks.slack.com","discord.com","transfer.sh","file.io","0x0.st")
| join kind=inner gyp_node_children on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (ProcSpawnTime .. ProcSpawnTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes, ParentProcessCommandLine

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,

Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access

detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
